target_deliverables.notes: proj is Gluing.desc of the two Subtype.val maps (checked by rfl in the audit probe). EtaleGluing is an abbrev of Causal.Gluing (inclusion h₁) (inclusion h₂), and its topology is Gluing's quotient topology (rfl). proj_comp_ι₁/ι₂ and range_proj = U₁ ∪ U₂ hold with no topology. isLocalHomeomorph_proj (mathlib IsLocalHomeomorph) assumes U₁, U₂, A open, as the target does. The codRestrict form is a surjective local homeomorphism onto ↥(U₁ ∪ U₂). secondCountableTopology is an extra.

injective_proj_iff : Injective π ↔ U₁ ∩ U₂ ⊆ A, with no topology and no hypothesis on A. isOpenEmbedding_proj / exists_homeomorph hold under U₁ ∩ U₂ ⊆ A. The fibres: {ι₁ x, ι₂ x} over U₁ ∩ U₂, encard 2 off A, a singleton over (U₁ ∪ U₂) ∖ (U₁ ∩ U₂ ∖ A), empty off U₁ ∪ U₂.

t2Space_iff assumes only [T2Space M] and IsOpen A (U₁, U₂ need not be open, which is correct). It goes through Gluing.t2Space_iff_forall_not_isCorrespondingBoundaryPair (GluingHausdorff.lean:307); its T2 hypotheses on U₁, U₂ come from M as subtypes. The condition U₁ ∩ U₂ ∩ closure_M A ⊆ A is exactly 'A closed in U₁ ∩ U₂', since the closure in a subspace is the subspace meet the ambient closure. t2Space_iff_isClosed states it verbatim as IsClosed (val ⁻¹' A) in ↥(U₁ ∩ U₂). isCorrespondingBoundaryPair_iff gives the pairs (x, x), x ∈ U₁ ∩ U₂ ∩ closure A ∖ A, as the target asks. t2Space_iff_eq_connectedComponentIn: IsOpen A, IsPreconnected A and x ∈ A (so A is connected) are enough, and the statement is right. ⇒: A is open, relatively closed and connected, so it is the component of x. ⇐: a component is relatively closed (insert y A is preconnected when y ∈ closure A). t2Space_connectedComponentIn assumes T2, locally connected M and U₁, U₂ open, as the target does. The audit probe instantiates it at ℝ ∖ {0}, x = 1, so it is not vacuous. subset_of_t2Space (any M) and eq_inter_of_t2Space are extras and correct.

glue : EtaleGluing h₁ h₂ → β is Gluing.desc (u₁ ∘ val) (u₂ ∘ val), so the glued function is defined on E. exists_glue_eq_comp_proj_iff : (∃ v : M → β, ũ = v ∘ π) ↔ EqOn u₁ u₂ (U₁ ∩ U₂) is 'factors through π' stated correctly (v on all of M is equivalent, since π lands in U₁ ∪ U₂). The optional glueSolutions form is checked in Probe.lean: the example elaborates with glueSolutions ⟨U₁, hU₁⟩ u₁ u₂ in place of the explicit if, so the two are definitionally equal.

punctured_witness instantiates t2Space_iff, t2Space_iff_eq_connectedComponentIn, isLocalHomeomorph_proj, not_injective_and_not_descends and both directions of exists_glue_eq_comp_proj_iff, at the target's data: U₁ = U₂ = ℝ∖{0}, A = Ioi 0, u₁ = 0, u₂ = 1_{Iio 0}. branching_witness instantiates isLocalHomeomorph_proj, isCorrespondingBoundaryPair_iff and subset_of_t2Space at U₁ = U₂ = ℝ, A = Ioi 0. punctured_not_isPreconnected instantiates not_isPreconnected_inter. None of the data is trivial.

The checklist rows are true: every weakening is real and none strengthens the target. SCOPE discloses that A is any open set and is never read as the MCGHD, and that the smooth structure and the PDE are not formalized. findings.what: The finding is right in substance. Injectivity of π (U₁ ∩ U₂ ⊆ A, so a connected overlap given :850) and agreement on the whole overlap (descent of ũ, exists_glue_eq_comp_proj_iff) are distinct, and the title conflates them. 'agree ⇒ injective' fails as topology (punctured_witness, last conjunct). For the planner it is under-stated in two ways. (a) The other direction of the title holds: π injective ⇒ u₁ = u₂ on U₁ ∩ U₂, in one line from injective_proj_iff and EqOn u₁ u₂ A (checked in the audit probe). (b) The counterexample is topological. Its A is a component chosen by hand with u₁ = u₂ = 0 everywhere; it is not the MCGHD of two GHDs of a quasilinear equation. Whether two GHDs can agree on all of a disconnected overlap is a causal/PDE question this module does not decide: if they cannot, the title's iff holds in ERS's setting; ERS Lemmas 4.70/4.72 give connected overlaps under extra hypotheses. So 'false as topology' is accurate, but it must not reach the planner as 'the title is false'.
findings.fix: Reword finding 2: 'The title's ⇒ (injective ⇒ agreement on U₁ ∩ U₂) holds. Its ⇐ (agreement ⇒ injective) does not follow from the topology (punctured_witness), and in the causal setting it is open: it would need that two GHDs agreeing on their overlap have a connected overlap. Restate the title as the split: π injective ⇔ U₁ ∩ U₂ = MCGHD (⇔ connected overlap, given :850); ũ descends ⇔ u₁ = u₂ on U₁ ∩ U₂ (ERS global uniqueness for the pair); record agreement ⇒ injective as a causal question.'

findings.what: "So ':850' is load-bearing for 'a manifold', which ERS do not say" can be read as saying ERS omit the component identification. They state it in :852 itself ('glueing them together along the MCGHD (which equals the connected component of U₁ ∩ U₂ which contains the initial data hypersurface)'). What ERS do not say is that the Hausdorff property of the glued space depends on A being the whole component (t2Space_iff, branching_witness). The mathematics of the finding is correct.
findings.fix: Reword: 'ERS state the component identification (:852's parenthetical, from :850) but do not say that the Hausdorff property of the glued manifold depends on it; gluing along a smaller open set with a frontier point in U₁ ∩ U₂ is non-Hausdorff (t2Space_iff, branching_witness).'
